Melinda Bandalaria has advised 21 theses in this repository between 2018 and 2026. They have an advisee in the latest year recorded in the repository, 2026. Their supervision patterns show a diverse range of research interests, with the most frequent sub-topics being communication studies (9), culture and identity (7), community development (4), social media (3), language and literacy (3), business and entrepreneurship (3), agriculture and food (2), public health and COVID-19 (2), and youth and family (2). They have also supervised work related to environment and sustainability (1).

Based on the supervised theses, Bandalaria's research focus involves examining how communication interacts with various social, cultural, and economic structures. In the area of communication studies, they have supervised research on developer communication in extreme programming, communication for social acceptability in ecotourism, and the use of the Communication for Development (C4D) model in corporate social responsibility. Their work also covers communication strategies for community mobilization and the communication of public policy.

Bandalaria has a significant presence in research concerning culture and identity. Supervised topics include the transmission of Tausug oral traditions, the formation of reader identity through eBook reading habits, and how academic institutions communicate core values for character formation. They have also overseen studies on how indigenous people learners construct the meaning of education through social interaction and the role of beauty pageants as platforms for advocacy communication.

In the realms of public health and social issues, Bandalaria has supervised research on digital community building among Filipino gay men living with HIV, the effectiveness of public messaging for HIV communication, and the vulnerability of overseas Filipino workers to fake news on social media. Their supervision also extends to community development and economic recovery, including studies on mobilizing overseas workers for financial stability and communication for sustained volunteerism in pawikan conservation.

The adviser has also supervised work involving social media, such as content creation for not-for-profit virtual communities and the impact of social media on information disorder among senior high school students. Additionally, they have overseen research in agriculture and food, specifically regarding the lived experiences of agricultural extension workers during crises and the evolving professional identity of development communication practitioners in the agricultural sector. While they have no articles of their own in this repository, their extensive supervision history demonstrates a broad engagement with development communication and its application across various sectors of Philippine society.
